title: The first press of play on a long recording does not hitch
goal: On a five minute recording, the first time you press play the window stops answering for about a sixth of a second before the picture moves. Later presses are fine. A press should never hold the window that long.
notes: Found while fixing starting-an-export-does-not-freeze-the-window. Repro (temp walk: openLongRetinaTalk, wait 1.5, videoPause, wait 0.6, key l, wait 0.5, key k, wait 0.3, key l, wait 0.5, key k): Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/exstall/lonly.json --no-build, run twice. Output: first L wait -> "0.5s, never went quiet (14 of 14 slices busy); mainBusy 410.6ms over 269 passes, longest 156.7ms" and "... longest 149.3ms"; second L -> longest 34.6ms / 22.0ms. During an export the same first press read longest 67.4ms. Not yet sampled: run sample(1) on the probe across the first L to find the long pass.
acceptance: On the five minute Retina sample, the first L press after opening keeps the longest main thread stretch under 50 ms (today about 150 ms)
The cause is named in the task log with the measurement that shows it
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on

log.note: Reproduced: /tmp/firstplay/walk.json (openLongRetinaTalk, videoPause, L, K, L, K). First L longest pass 104.8ms, second 24.9ms.

Cause (timed with temporary CACurrentMediaTime marks, removed): the 105.7ms pass was the L press itself, 99.5ms of it in startAudio. First-time only: creating DocumentAudioPlayer (AVAudioEngine() + mainMixerNode) 44.1ms; engine.start() 30.6ms (11.0ms warm); AVAudioFile open + attach + prepare + schedule about 16ms (8ms warm). The audio mix plan and headroom reading were NOT the cost (under 3ms). sample(1) and a Time Profiler trace missed it because the main thread was mostly blocked on coreaudiod, not running.

Fix: DocumentAudioPlayer keeps only the arithmetic on the main actor; the engine, files and nodes live in DocumentAudioEngine on its own serial queue (FIFO so play/stop order holds; walks read engine state with queue.sync). The engine is built on that queue when the timeline of a document with sound opens (EditorState.readyAudio from TimelineDock's task). First L now 19.7/18.8/18.6/19.3/19.1ms across runs; new walk first-press-of-play-answers-at-once-walk fails on the old code (98.2ms) and passes on the new.

Left rough, not filed: (1) opening the five minute Retina talk itself holds the window about 430ms in one pass (the wait right after openLongRetinaTalk); not investigated, no open task covers it. (2) the picture's clock starts at the press while the sound starts after engine start plus its 80ms lead, so sound may trail picture slightly on any press; unmeasured, so not filed as a bug.

The first L on the five minute Retina talk now peaks at 18.6 to 19.7 ms on the main thread (was 105 to 157). Cause: the press built and started the audio engine on the main thread (44 ms to make it, 31 ms to start it, about 16 ms to wire it). The engine now lives on its own queue and is made when the timeline opens. New walk first-press-of-play-answers-at-once-walk (Next defaults, fails at 50 ms) passes, and fails at 98 ms on the old code. Six sound walks and Scripts/test.sh (10,561 tests) pass. Commit cd4e5d1f.
